paper_title: SELF-CONTRADICTION HALLUCINATIONS OF LLMs: EVALUATION, DETECTION AND MITIGATION

experiments.research_goal: To evaluate the effectiveness of self-contradiction detection and mitigation in LLMs, and to develop a robust method for identifying and removing contradictions in generated text.

methods.name: Self-contradiction Triggering
methods.description: Algorithm 1 is used to trigger self-contradictions in the generated text, which is then evaluated for consistency.

methods.name: Self-contradiction Detection
methods.description: A detection method is employed to identify contradictions in the generated text, using a combination of retrieval-based and classification metrics.

datasets.name: MainTestSet
datasets.description: A test set consisting of 360 descriptions spanning four gLMs and 30 diverse entities, used to evaluate the effectiveness of self-contradiction detection and mitigation.

key_results: The generated descriptions are long, with an average of 7.3 to 12.5 sentences per description.
The average perplexity of the generated descriptions is measured using OPT-1.3B.
The detection of self-contradictions achieves an F1 score of approximately 80%.
experiments.conclusion: It is open to explore the potential of fine-tuning smaller open-source LMs to achieve high performance as aLM or even training LMs to avoid generating contradictory content. Finally, we note that other kinds of hallucinations than self-contradictions exist. For example, LMs can consistently generate incorrect content.
experiments.limitations: Open-source LMs (Llama2-70B-Chat and Vicuna-13B) show limitations, particularly in low detection recall and inability to effectively remove self-contradictions. Fortunately, state-of-the-art open-source instruction-tuned LMs have substantially advanced in recent months, with Llama2-70B-Chat (released in late July 2023, current state-of-the-art) significantly outperforming Vicuna-13B (version 1.1, released in early May 2023 and then state-of-the-art according to LMSYS (2023b)).
evidence: The detection achieves a high F1 score of $\sim 80\%$ .
Table 2 also shows the average perplexity of the descriptions, measured using OPT-1.3B (Zhang et al., 2022).
In Table 2, we show that the generated descriptions are long, consisting of between 7.3 and 12.5 sentences on average.
Our evaluation highlights the significance of self-contradiction.

research_problem: Self-contradiction hallucination detection and mitigation in LLMs
research_problem_description: Self-contradiction hallucination refers to the generation of inconsistent or logically conflicting information by large language models (LLMs) during open-domain text generation and question answering. This phenomenon poses a significant challenge in ensuring the reliability and trustworthiness of LLM outputs, particularly in critical applications where accuracy is paramount. The paper addresses the problem of identifying and mitigating these contradictions to enhance the quality and consistency of LLM-generated text.
